Finding.Text: No document says how an open change is finished once the kernel has moved ahead of the pin. Probed on a HEAD clone with the pin at 0.2.0 and C-0004 open: run and close refuse "run grace5 upgrade", and upgrade and upgrade --plan refuse "open changes: C-0004-upgrade-command", so the new kernel can neither finish the change nor upgrade past it; the only ways out are the previous kernel (this checkout at the previous tag, since pilots run the kernel from the checkout) or abandoning the change, and the same holds when the pin is ahead, where upgrade names the open changes although closing them with this kernel is impossible. upgrade.md says "(the owner closes or waits)" and both skills say a refusal "means the state is behind the kernel: run grace5 upgrade first, which needs every change closed", which, read by the agent executing that open change, is advice that cannot succeed. The behaviour is what Change and D2 require and the kernel is correct; the sentence that names the previous kernel as the way to close is missing from upgrade.md, from the execute skill and from the prepare skill. For the author.

An unreadable pin has a behaviour no document or help text states. readPin throws on a file that is not a dotted numeric version (probed with "banana" and with an empty file): check, run, close, init and upgrade then print "grace5: .grace5/kernel-version is not a version: banana" (or "empty") from the top-level handler of cli.ts, exit 1, and status prints "kernel: 0.3.0, state: unreadable (.grace5/kernel-version is not a version: banana)". commands.md lists the fixed phrases the pin adds and upgrade.md lists the status first lines (equal, behind, ahead, none); neither names the unreadable case, and the line is not a refused: line. The outcome is safe, nothing is written and the kernel does not operate on the state, so this is a documentation gap rather than a defect; a reader of commands.md or a test cannot rely on the phrase.

UP-07 asserts that the number of refreshed: lines equals twice the number of links the plan prints (versionsOf(upgrade) minus one, two existing directories), but the kernel refreshes the skills on a step only, not on a bump: applyUpgrade calls refreshSkills inside the link.kind === "step" branch, as upgrade.md states ("Every step also refreshes", "a pin bump: nothing but the pin changes"). The assertion holds today because the chain from 0.1.0 is two steps and no bump; the first kernel version that adds a bump to that chain will fail UP-07 for a reason that is not a kernel defect. The expected count should be twice the number of step: lines.
